title: Assess your organisation's strengths and gaps
summary: A strategy only works if the organisation can deliver it. Be honest about what you are good at, what you lack and what you could build or buy.

beginner: List what your team and company do well, with examples.
List the skills, systems or data you would need but don't have.
Ask a few colleagues to challenge the list.
Mark which gaps matter most for the core challenge.
Note which gaps could be filled quickly and which take years.
intermediate: Compare your strengths with competitors and alternatives.
Decide which capabilities make you different and which are commodities.
Estimate the cost and time to close the biggest gaps.
experienced: Assess capabilities across the portfolio and shared platforms.
Decide where to invest in people, where to partner and where to stop.
Build the capability plan into the strategy, not after it.

toolExamples.miro: Map capabilities as strengths and gaps on one board.
toolExamples.google-docs: Score each capability for importance and current strength.

definitionOfDone: Time and cost to close the top gaps estimated
pitfalls: Ignoring how long it takes to build skills
